whatItDoes: Calculates the maturity value and interest earned on a lump-sum fixed deposit. It compounds your deposit at the stated annual rate over the tenure, with monthly, quarterly, or annual compounding.
whyItExists: Fixed deposits are a safe, predictable savings vehicle, but the maturity amount depends heavily on the rate and how often interest is compounded. This calculator makes the final value easy to see before you lock in.
whoShouldUse: Savers comparing deposit options, investors laddering fixed deposits, and anyone planning a lump-sum savings goal.
useCases: Estimate the maturity value of a deposit
Plan a lump-sum savings toward a goal
See how the rate changes the final amount
Compare tenures to pick the right lock-in period
Model a ladder of deposits with different maturities
instructions: Enter the annual interest rate as a percent
Read the maturity value and interest earned
Compare two rates or tenures side by side
Check the maturity date so you know when the funds become available
examples: $100,000 at 6.5% for 5 years, annual → ≈ $137,010 — monthly compounding earns slightly more
bestPractices: Compare rates across banks, not just one offer
Consider how early-withdrawal penalties affect liquidity
Check if the rate is fixed for the full tenure
Re-run with quarterly vs. monthly to see the difference
Understand that a longer tenure at a flat rate may not beat reinvesting at better rates
Match the deposit tenure to when you actually need the money
commonMistakes: Using a nominal rate instead of a compounding rate
Choosing a longer tenure without checking the interest
Forgetting tax on interest in some jurisdictions
Assuming penalties don't exist for early withdrawal
Assuming all banks compound at the same frequency
Renewing automatically without re-comparing the new rate
faq: What is compounding frequency? — How often interest is added to the principal (monthly, quarterly, or annually).
Is this tax advice? — No, interest may be taxable depending on your jurisdiction.
Can I withdraw early? — Usually with penalties that this tool does not model.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Which compounding frequency gives the highest return? — More frequent compounding (monthly) earns slightly more than quarterly or annual at the same nominal rate.
What is a deposit ladder? — Splitting money across deposits with different tenures so some matures each year, balancing rate and liquidity.
